These have been shown to be effective for induction therapy and maintenance in both ulcerative colitis and Crohn’s disease.6,17 The anti- integrin antibody natalizumab is effective in inducing remission in Crohn’s disease.18 Thalidomide, a tumour necrosis factor inhibitor, has also been tried in Crohn’s disease with some benefit,16,19 but another such inhibi- tor, pentoxifylline, was ineffective.20 • Metronidazole is useful in fistulising perineal Crohn’s disease and may be used in colonic Crohn’s disease. It is usually given for 3 months. Ciprofloxacin is an alterna- tive, and has also been given with metronidazole,21,22 al- though the combination may not be very well tolerated. There has been interest in the possible causal role of Mycobacterium paratuberculosis in Crohn’s disease,23 but a study of 2 years of antituberculous therapy with clarithromycin, rifabutin, and clofazimine in patients with Crohn’s disease found no evidence of sustained benefit, suggesting that the organism probably did not play a significant role.24 Antibacterials do not have a role in ulcerative colitis, except for infection prophylax- is in severe attacks. • Many other drugs are being or have been tried in IBD, including immunoglobulins, some interleukins, inter- ferons, ICAM-antisense oligonucleotides such as alica- forsen, the anti-CD3 antibody visilizumab, short-chain fatty acids, heparin, factor XIII, rosiglitazone, and ami- nosalicylic acid (4-aminosalicylic acid as opposed to 5- aminosalicylic acid). There have been some short-term responses to the anti-integrin antibody, MLN-02,25 and to the anti-interleukin-12 antibody, ABT-874.26 There is limited evidence of improvement in disease severity from the use of the granulocyte-macrophage colony- stimulating factor sargramostim,27 which is thought able to stimulate intestinal innate immune defence processes that may be impaired in Crohn’s disease. Nicotine has been tried in ulcerative colitis, based on the observation that the disease is rare in smokers. Studies have suggest- ed that nicotine, supplied via transdermal patch, may have benefit in active disease,28 although it is ineffective for maintenance.29 Rectal and oral formulations of nico- tine are under investigation. Nutritional and dietary therapies. Correction of nutritional deficiencies may be necessary in severe IBD, but dietary modification may also have thera- peutic effects.
